head: bailly_joseph

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE PAPER, NOT AN ARRIVAL. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1835-07-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: A letter was still waiting for this name at the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4, on or after the scene date, so the corpus puts somebody expecting them at Chicago at 1835-07-01.

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Bailly, Joseph' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.evidence_for: Honoré Gratien Joseph Bailly de Messein is a strong regional candidate, but lived at his Porter County homestead and died there in December 1835. A Chicago letter may reflect transit, not residence.
resident_research.evidence_against: Documented Porter County residence; no source links him to this letter.
resident_research.notes: Candidate facts remain unasserted until a source bridges the candidate to the historical record by more than name similarity.
resident_research.evidence_against: Bailly's household stood on the Little Calumet in Indiana, not in Chicago; a letter waiting at the Chicago post office is consistent with a trader who collected mail there and is not evidence of residence.
resident_research.summary: A same-name lead, recorded and NOT asserted.
resident_research.notes: candidate retained unasserted; no grade or placement moves

candidates.basis: Joseph Bailly the American Fur Company trader is licensed for the Lake Michigan trade in 1821 (Hurlbut) and Fergus's old-settler death notices print 'Bailly, Joseph, died, Baillytown, Ind., December 21, 1835, aged 61'.
conflicts: His household stood on the Little Calumet in Indiana; a letter waiting at the Chicago post office is what a trader who collected mail here leaves, not a residence.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
